newsitem.title: UK: High grade cobalt set to fall in 1997 - Macquarie.
newsitem.headline: High grade cobalt set to fall in 1997 - Macquarie.

text.p: High grade cobalt prices are likely to fall in 1997, Macquarie Equities Ltd said in their latest commodities report
Macquarie estimate that total world supplies in 1996 grew by 16.2 percent in 1996 and that supply exceeded demand by around 2,000 tonnes, allowing severely depleted stocks to rebuild.
"We believe that the erosion in prices will continue in the coming year as supply outstrips demand" Macquarie said.
"The main questions facing the market are not if, but when and by how much."
High prices of recent years were a reflection of the collapse in production from the traditionally dominant African producers.
Production from these producers (Zaire and Zambia) fell from 14,877 tonnes to 5,939 tonnes in 1994 before starting to rise again.
Macquarie believes potentially large increases in production could come from the recovery of cobalt from slag heaps.
They also said the other main source of cobalt supply is as a by product of nickel.
Production from this source is set to grow in the coming years as Queensland Nickel expands production and new hydrometallurgical plants kick into production.
